Alex: Heads-up — after rolling INT8 quantization + new slot packing to canary, we see expected memory reduction on KV (≈35-40%) but a reproducible accuracy delta on long-context evals (~1.4-1.8% decrease on convo-fidelity).
Alex: I profiled a 3h long-context replay with heavy reuse; paging shows increased page churn after ~45m. Suspect eviction hysteresis + quant noise interaction.
perf-bot: perf trace uploaded: /artifacts/kv/1729998888/trace.tar.gz : event counts: page_evict=1243, page_reclaim=1189, avg_residency_ms=463, int8_slots=72%, reuse_hit=0.64
Maria: Interesting. Did you run with the new compact-on-alloc change? That might change fragmentation distribution vs compact-on-evict.
Alex: compact-on-alloc=true in canary. Eviction policy: size_based with hysteresis 0.15 (15% tolerance).
Josh: Kernel note: when a page is hot but stored in INT8, we sometimes fall back to BF16 matmul path because of small vector alignment mismatch. That incurs an extra memcpy which can push pages over the eviction threshold during bursts.
Ravi: Repro instructions request: can you paste the exact run command + config? I'll spin a minimal repro.
Alex: Sure:
```
./run_canary --model redwood-7b-int8 --kv-config '{"compact_on_alloc":true,"eviction_policy":"size_based","hysteresis":0.15,"page_size":65536}' --replay-seconds 10800 --trace /tmp/trace
```
Alex: Heap tail from the run (snipped):
```
KV pages: total=3584, resident=1294, free_slots=210, avg_slot_size=448
page_churn_window(10m): evict=112, reuse_hit=0.62
quantized_errors: l2_delta_mean=0.0048, topk_shift=0.008
```
Maria: I ran a quick split test: compact-on-evict + hysteresis=0.05 -> memory reduction slightly worse (~30%) but accuracy loss gone (delta ~0.1%). Might be hysteresis sensitivity.
Sara: Can we try a simple eviction hysteresis schedule: start low (0.05) for first 30m warmup then ramp to 0.15? Should keep early reuse and avoid thrash.
Josh: Also try aligning page_size to kernel vector width: page_size=32768 vs 65536 changes memcpy patterns — that previously improved kernel staying on int8 path.
Ravi: I'm going to run three quick experiments on a dev node:
- A: compact-on-alloc + hysteresis 0.15 + page 65536 (current canary)
- B: compact-on-evict + hysteresis 0.05 + page 65536
- C: compact-on-alloc + hysteresis schedule (0.05->0.15) + page 32768
Ravi: ETA ~45m. Will post numeric diffs.
perf-bot: bench job queued: job_id=kv-exp-1729998888, nodes=2, expected=40m
Maria: Minor: we should capture kernel selection traces (which matmul path was used per page) — add "--trace-kernels" so we can correlate page residency vs kernel fallback.
Alex: Good call. Also record sample logits on the eval set each 30m so we can detect drift windows.
Ravi: Quick results (first 45m):
- A: mem_reduction=38%, reuse_hit=0.63, accuracy_delta=-1.6%
- B: mem_reduction=31%, reuse_hit=0.70, accuracy_delta=-0.2%
- C: mem_reduction=36%, reuse_hit=0.66, accuracy_delta=-0.3%
Ravi: Kernel traces show A had ~22% of matmuls falling back to BF16 path during burst periods; C reduced that to ~8%.
Josh: That confirms kernel fallback hypothesis. The alignment + hysteresis schedule reduces fallbacks and restrains eviction thrash.
Sara: Actionable: revert compact-on-alloc for next canary, or keep it but apply hysteresis schedule + page_size=32768 for models where int8 kernels are fragile.
Maria: I'll open a PR with a new toggled config: kv.hysteresis_warmup_ms and kv.page_size_hint and add kernel-trace logging flag.
Alex: Filing perf regression ticket with numbers + attaching traces. Tagging infra for canary rollout pause until we validate.
Sara: Thanks — please add a quick note to the release channel when the PR is ready so we don't accidentally promote. :eyes:
Alex: Will do.
Maria: Nice investigative work y'all.
